    NASA Artemis II mission successfully launched on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT     from Kennedy Space Center, Florida. The SLS rocket successfully propelled four astronauts into Earth orbit to begin a 10-day mission around the moon. The Orion capsule is currently operating normally in orbit after passing initial checks. 
    This video shows a previous rocket launch, similar to the one discussed:
    47s
    Spaceflight Now
    YouTube• Jun 19, 2025
    Key Details: 
    • Mission: Artemis II, the first crewed mission to the Moon since 1972.
    • Launch Time: 6:35 p.m. EDT, Wednesday, April 1, 2026.
    • Location: Launch Pad 39B, Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
    • Crew: Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Hammock Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
    • Status: Successful liftoff with crew currently orbiting Earth.
    • Follow Live: You can track the mission and view official updates via RocketLaunch.Live. 
    The crew is now scheduled for a 10-day journey, including a "translunar injection burn" to head toward the moon.
